simple.meaning: בַּעֲלָה (baʻălâh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a mistress.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at 1 Samuel 28:7. The surrounding context includes family line.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בַּעֲלָה (H1172) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: בַּעֲלָה (baʻălâh) / H1172 is traced through 1 Samuel 28:7, 1 Kings 17:17, Nahum 3:4 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Then Saul said to his servants, “Seek for me a woman who has a familiar spirit, that I may go to her, and inquire of her.”

timeline.evidenceText: Then Saul said to his servants, “Seek for me a woman who has a familiar spirit, that I may go to her, and inquire of her.”
Then Saul said to his servants, “Seek for me a woman who has a familiar spirit, that I may go to her, and inquire of her.”

because of the multitude of the prostitution of the alluring prostitute, the mistress of witchcraft, who sells nations through her prostitution, and families through her witchcraft.
